AI Literacy — Level 1
Redesigned Storyboard and Voiceover Script
Design principle: one clear learning point per instructional slide, purposeful interaction, minimal on-screen copy, and narration that carries the explanation.
Design decisions
The sequence is intentionally linear: Understanding AI → capabilities and limits → AI at work → responsible AI → data, privacy and security → prompting → AI agents and Atlas → assessment.
Related ideas are separated when they represent different learning points. The learner sees less text at once and the narrator carries the explanation.
AWARE is introduced once as the course mental model and then used as a subtle design cue rather than repeatedly re-teaching the framework.
Knowledge checks use separate layer slides so the Storyline build can map directly to the storyboard.
The Atlas section is a short experience, not a full tool course. Exact interface steps should be captured from the approved Atlas environment rather than invented in the storyboard.
The assessment is scenario-based and focuses on judgment rather than recall.

Storyline build guidance
Use the layer slides as direct build references for the preceding knowledge check or assessment slide.
Keep feedback concise and actionable. Avoid repeating the entire teaching point on every feedback layer.
Use one consistent interaction pattern for knowledge checks so the learner focuses on the decision rather than learning a new interaction each time.
For Atlas, replace the generic screen-recording placeholder with the actual approved Atlas interface. Keep the narration focused on task definition, instructions, context, testing, and review.
Keep on-screen text minimal. Do not place the full voiceover on the slide.
Use the same visual grammar throughout: strong heading, one main idea, two or three supporting visual elements, and a consistent footer.
Additional design recommendations

Audience and runtime: Confirm the target audience. Several examples (promotions, disciplinary actions, candidates, employee recommendations) lean toward HR and people managers; add examples from other functions if the audience is broader. Add the estimated duration on slides 1 and 2 once the voiceover is timed.

Objective alignment: Objective 1 (use AI effectively and understand limits) is taught on slides 5 to 28 and assessed by Q1, Q2 and Q6. Objective 2 (use AI responsibly and protect information) is taught on slides 29 to 44 and assessed by Q3, Q4 and Q7. Objective 3 (prompting) is taught on slides 45 to 54 and assessed by Q5. Objective 4 (AI agents, added) is taught on slides 55 to 62 and assessed by Q8. Bias and fairness and intellectual property have no assessment items; consider adding them.

Mastery rules (confirm before build): A suggested default is an 80 percent pass mark, two attempts, randomized option order, and routing a learner who does not pass back to the sections that match the questions missed. Decide whether questions are drawn from a larger pool.
LMS tracking: Specify what is reported (completion, score, time) and the format (SCORM or xAPI).

Sources: Anchor the definitions of AI, bias, hallucination, and AI agent to a recognized source such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or the OECD definition of an AI system, and keep a definitions log for reviewers.
Versioning: Name a content owner and set a review cadence (suggested every 6 months). Keep tool-specific content (slides 55 to 62) separable so only those slides need refreshing.
Reviews and pilot: Obtain Legal, Privacy, Security and HR sign-off on their sections before build, and pilot with a small group of real learners to find confusing questions.

Accessibility: Specify alt text, reading and focus order, keyboard operation for every selectable card and hotspot, captions and a transcript, sufficient contrast, and no meaning carried by color alone. Test the reveal animations with a screen reader.
Narration: Where the voiceover repeats the on-screen text word for word, use it to add an example or explanation instead. Add pronunciation notes for LLM and AWARE.
Build consistency: Use one slide master and one feedback-layer template, limit knowledge-check retries to one, and document the score variable and the triggers that feed the results slide (79a).
